def _report_failure(watcher: Studi0Watcher, error: BaseException) -> None:
    """Report ``error`` on stderr unless this watch already has."""
    signature = f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}"
    if signature in watcher.reported_failures:
        return
    watcher.reported_failures.add(signature)
    print(
        f"studi0: could not read the project's build artifacts, "
        f"keeping the last good view — {signature}",
        file=sys.stderr,
        flush=True,
    )

intent.value: Says once, on stderr, that studi0 could not read the project this time — and stays silent every later time the same thing goes wrong, so a console watching a broken project stays readable. Distinctness is the exception's type and message together: a different file failing, or the same file failing differently, is a different thing worth hearing about.

The body of the watching thread: wait out the poll interval, take a reading, repeat — and end the moment a stop is requested. Waiting on the stop event rather than sleeping is what makes a shutdown immediate instead of up-to-one-tick slow.

The poll that keeps a studi0 session honest between builds: roughly four times a second it re-reads the project's build artifacts and republishes the session's reading only when the project actually said something new. It runs on a daemon thread so an interrupted studi0 dies with its server; it treats a build caught half-written as a reason to keep the last good reading and look again, not as a reason to fall over; and it reports each distinct failure to stderr once, never once per tick.
